issue.title: enhancement: project-skills-discovery reads every SKILL.md unconditionally across 5 agents with no index-size budget

timeline.body:
The affected scope is broader than the five agents listed in this issue. At commit a2331c0, 21 distinct agent definitions contain this behavior through two paths:

5 agents import the shared discovery reference: debugger, executor, phase-researcher, planner, and verifier.

16 additional agents repeat the instruction inline: code-fixer, code-reviewer, codebase-mapper, doc-verifier, doc-writer, eval-auditor, integration-checker, intel-updater, nyquist-auditor, pattern-mapper, plan-checker, roadmapper, security-auditor, ui-auditor, ui-checker, and ui-researcher.


Consequently, changing only project-skills-discovery.md would leave 16 agents with the existing inline instruction. The fix should cover both paths, ideally consolidating the duplicated instructions.


That on its own is an inconsistency worth fixing.

@forfrossen Thank you for bringing this to our attention. Please feel free to take on the work for this enhancement/fix. Otherwise, it may not be taken care of until someone has the time to get to it.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Triage disposition: approved — both directions

Approved by the maintainer, covering **both** directions as filed:

1. **Relevance-filter the index read** — scope step 3 to task-relevant skills rather than reading every `SKILL.md`.
2. **Add an index size budget plus an author-facing lint warning** — extending `scripts/lint-skill-deps.cjs`.

Verified during triage on `next`:

- Step 3 of `gsd-core/references/project-skills-discovery.md:8` is unconditional as quoted ("Read `SKILL.md` for each skill"), with no relevance filter at the index level; lazy loading applies only to `rules/*.md` at step 4.
- Exactly five agents `@`-include that reference: `gsd-executor`, `gsd-planner`, `gsd-verifier`, `gsd-debugger`, `gsd-phase-researcher`. This matches the report's corrected mechanism.
- The "~130 lines" figure in step 3 is descriptive prose, not an enforced budget.
- No prior denial applies. The nearest keyword neighbour in `.out-of-scope/`, `general-purpose-agent-prompt-skills.md` (#2614), denies standalone agent-discipline prompt modules as core skills and its own scope-boundary section explicitly exempts changes to an existing first-party agent's behavior at a specific loop step.

**Constraint recorded with the approval** — carried from the report's own breaking-change analysis: relevance scoping changes what an agent sees on spawn, so it must preserve the ability to reach any skill's `rules/*.md` on demand. No skill may become unreachable as a result of being filtered out of the index read.

**Not approved by this decision:** path-scoped / per-role discovery. The report names it as a possible larger follow-up and explicitly does not ask for it here; it remains unfiled.

Labels: `approved-enhancement` added, `needs-triage` removed.

It’s worse than expected: a Vercel-specific workaround became GSD’s general skill-discovery policy.

At the revision discussed here (a2331c0), the instruction reaches 21 agent definitions: five through the shared reference and sixteen through inline copies. Updating the shared file alone would leave most occurrences intact. This concerns unconditional project discovery; configured agent_skills injection is a separate mechanism. (Scope correction, issue scope)

The origin is get-shit-done gsd-build/get-shit-done#672, which explicitly describes vercel-react-best-practices and vercel-composition-patterns. Their particular layout supplied the assumptions carried into GSD: small SKILL.md indexes of roughly 130 lines, individual skill-internal rules/*.md files, and large compiled AGENTS.md files to avoid.

The subsequent history explains how this spread:

The original fix added the pattern to four agents. Four days later, the verifier change explicitly justified another copy as alignment with the existing pattern.

By April, #2150 called it the standard Project skills block and treated its absence as missing skills awareness. #2152 extended it to nine more agents and added tests checking its presence.

#2362 subsequently extracted it from five agents into a shared reference, explicitly preserving its behavior.


Both April PRs identify themselves as generated with Claude Code. The stated maintenance goals—consistency, coverage, and deduplication—help explain the propagation: later changes took the existing implementation as the project convention and carried its assumptions forward.

Those assumptions do not describe the general Agent Skills specification. Discovery loads metadata; activation loads the SKILL.md body; supporting resources load as needed. A skill may use rules/, but neither that directory nor a 130-line index is a universal contract. references/ is an explicitly documented resource convention.

The current instruction also disregards native loading controls. Codex supports disabling individual skills, while Claude supports visibility and automatic-invocation restrictions. A blanket filesystem read can therefore reintroduce content intentionally excluded from automatic loading. Absence from a native catalog does not necessarily mean failed discovery.

In the local Codex planner, executor, and checker transcripts I examined, skill metadata was already present before GSD discovery read every local SKILL.md; some resulting outputs were truncated. A commenter had already raised native relevant-skill loading in the original issue.

I therefore think the fix should preserve harness ownership of discovery, activation, and user configuration across all delivery paths, and follow each selected skill’s actual resource references. Relevance filtering and size warnings can help, but they do not resolve that ownership conflict by themselves.

@forfrossen thank you. Both points hold up, and one of them widens the fix surface further than 21.

**Scope, re-counted on `next` @ b90eef28e:** 5 agents `@`-include `references/project-skills-discovery.md` (debugger, executor, phase-researcher, planner, verifier), and 16 more carry the instruction inline, exactly the 16 you listed. On top of that, **15 `agents/*.compact.md` variants** carry the same inline copy (every one of the 16 except `plan-checker`). So the fix touches **36 agent files**, not 5. A fix that only edits the shared reference would leave 31 copies unchanged. The fix should consolidate the inline copies onto the shared reference first, so the approved behavior change lands in one place instead of 36.

**On harness ownership:** agreed that the relevance filter and size budget (the approved scope) do not settle who owns discovery and activation. A blanket filesystem read can bring back a skill the user deliberately hid from native auto-loading. That concern is real, and it is broader than this issue. trek-e's approval explicitly left path-scoped and per-role discovery unapproved, so I'll keep this issue to the approved scope plus the 36-file consolidation. The ownership question should go to its own issue for a maintainer decision, not ride along here. If you'd like to file it, your origin trace (get-shit-done #672, then #2150 / #2152 / #2362) is the evidence it needs.

Carried from the approval into any PR: relevance scoping must keep every skill's `rules/*.md` reachable on demand. No skill may become unreachable because the index read filtered it out.

> *Generated by AI during triage; reviewed and posted by a human maintainer (@davesienkowski).*

issue.title: enhancement: let runtimes with native skill loading own project-skill discovery; keep GSD's blanket read as the fallback

timeline.body:
Thanks @davesienkowski — I'll take this on, scoped to the approved directions plus the 36-file consolidation. Preparing it surfaced three points; the first changes where direction 2 should land.

**1. Direction 2 cannot live in `scripts/lint-skill-deps.cjs`.** That script scans gsd-core's own `commands/gsd/*.md` (line 37). A size budget there never sees a consumer project's `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/`, so it reaches neither project skill authors nor GSD users. When I raised this on Discord, the intent was a user-facing signal: a GSD user currently cannot see what the discovery read costs per spawn. Proposal: implement direction 2 as a `/gsd-health` warning (next free `W0xx`) that reports the number of project skills and total `SKILL.md` lines the discovery read broadcasts per spawn, against a configurable threshold. It behaves the same in every runtime.

**2. Compact variants conflate the two mechanisms.** `codebase-mapper`, `security-auditor`, `ui-researcher` and `eval-auditor` (`*.compact.md`) attribute the blanket read to `agent-skills-bootstrap.md`, which is the configured `agent_skills` path. Compact variants are served only to non-Claude runtimes (`src/init.cts:4314-4320`). The consolidation removes the conflation.

**3. Skill content now reaches an agent through up to three paths** (`next` @ b90eef28e):

| Path | Since | Loads | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery instruction | gsd-build/get-shit-done#672 (2026-02-19) | full `SKILL.md` of every project skill | all runtimes; 21 agents + 15 compact variants |
| `agent_skills` injection | #1355 (2026-03-24) | full `SKILL.md` of configured skills | all runtimes; per role |
| Native skill loading | #1261 (2026-06-15) granted `Skill` to agent_skills consumers (20 of 35 canonical agents today) | metadata; body on invocation | runtime-dependent |

The bootstrap dedup guard (`agent-skills-bootstrap.md`, step 1) only keeps injection from running twice. Nothing stops discovery from re-reading an injected skill, so a configured project skill's body is loaded twice per spawn in every runtime. I'd treat "discovery skips skills already present in the `<agent_skills>` block" as part of direction 1's relevance filtering.

Whether discovery should run at all where a runtime loads skills natively is the ownership question. I've filed it separately as suggested: #4948.

PR plan: (a) consolidate the 31 inline copies onto `references/project-skills-discovery.md`; (b) relevance filter including the injection dedup, keeping every skill's resources reachable on demand per the approval constraint; (c) direction 2 per your answer below.

Two confirmations before I start: is `/gsd-health` the right home for direction 2, and is the injection dedup acceptable under direction 1?

@forfrossen thanks, and thanks for filing #4948. Both points check out on `next` @ af822a802.

**1. Direction 2's home.** Agreed. `scripts/lint-skill-deps.cjs:37` defaults to gsd-core's own `commands/gsd`, so a budget there never sees a consumer's `.claude/skills/`. A `/gsd-health` warning reaches the people the budget is for. `W030` is unused on `next`. One suggestion: start with a fixed threshold constant rather than a new config key. A key adds a schema entry and a docs surface, and it can come later if someone needs to tune it. This moves direction 2 away from the file named in the approval, so @trek-e, please confirm the relocation before the PR lands.

**2. Injection dedup.** From my side, yes, it fits direction 1. A skill already delivered through `agent_skills` stays reachable, so skipping it in discovery meets the approval's constraint. One ordering trap: in the agents themselves, discovery runs before the bootstrap self-load (e.g. `agents/gsd-executor.md:65` then `:69`). On paths where the orchestrator did not inject, such as `/gsd-autonomous`'s `Skill()` delegation (`workflows/autonomous.md`, "No per-delegation injection is needed here") or Cursor, no `<agent_skills>` block exists when discovery runs. A check keyed on that block would miss, and a configured skill that lives under `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` would still be read twice. Keying the dedup on the configured set (`query agent-skills <type>`) avoids that. Please leave the ADR-1866 injection contract and `tests/agent-skills.test.cjs` unchanged.

> *Generated by AI during triage; reviewed and posted by a human maintainer (@davesienkowski).*

Status update: the implementation is on my fork, branch [`enhance/4649-bound-project-skills-discovery`](https://github.com/forfrossen/gsd-core/tree/enhance/4649-bound-project-skills-discovery), based on `next` @ af822a802. Four points differ from what we discussed, so I'm asking for confirmation before opening the PR.

**As discussed**
- **Consolidation.** All 21 discovery agents and their 15 compact variants @-include `references/project-skills-discovery.md`, as REQ-BOILER-03 already required. This also removes the conflation: in most inline copies, the `agent_skills` line sat between the "Project skills" heading and its numbered steps.
- **Direction 1.** The index read covers only each skill's frontmatter (`name`, `description`). A full SKILL.md is read only when its `description` fits the task, and a skipped skill stays available for a later read. A SKILL.md without a description is still read in full, as before.
- **Direction 2** is a `/gsd-health` warning, `W030`, with a fixed constant and no config key.

**Four points that need confirmation**
1. **The dedup reads the configured set via `config-get`, not `query agent-skills`.** It is keyed on the configured set, as suggested. But on non-Claude runtimes with nothing configured, `query agent-skills <type>` returns the agent's whole persona (the #2454 fallback; 46,951 bytes for `gsd-executor` on OpenCode), which the bootstrap already loads once. `gsd_run config-get agent_skills.<type> --default "[]"` returns only the list. Limitation: without a project `config.json`, it does not see `agent_skills` from `~/.gsd/defaults.json`, and the skill is read twice, as today. Only agents that self-load skip anything, so no configured skill becomes unreachable. ADR-1866 and `tests/agent-skills.test.cjs` are unchanged.
2. **The steps no longer encode the layout of the gsd-build/get-shit-done#672 skill pack.** Step 4 ("load `rules/*.md`") and step 5 ("Do NOT load full `AGENTS.md`") came from that pack; the Agent Skills spec defines neither. Resources now load through "files a SKILL.md references (for example under `references/`, `scripts/`, or `rules/`)". `rules/` stays reachable, as the approval requires, because the gsd-build/get-shit-done#672 pack's SKILL.md references its rules files itself. The 21 role lines changed accordingly.
3. **I removed the AGENTS.md strip from `neutralizeAgentReferences`**, in both copies (`src/runtime-artifact-conversion.cts` and `bin/install.js`). It only served that step-5 sentence, and it left an empty numbered item ("5. ") in the discovery steps on Codex, Copilot, Antigravity, Kimi, OpenCode and Kilo. A guard test fails if an agent or reference reintroduces an instruction not to load AGENTS.md.
4. **W030 checks each skill instead of a total.** After direction 1, the per-spawn read is frontmatter only, so a total-lines budget no longer measures the cost. W030 warns for a project SKILL.md that has no `description` (read in full on every spawn) or more than 500 lines (the Agent Skills guideline). @trek-e, this is also the relocation from `scripts/lint-skill-deps.cjs` that needs your confirmation.

**Verification.** I ran the full suite on `next` and on the branch in the same environment: 40,088 vs. 40,142 tests (+54 new) and the same 19 failures (environment-dependent; they fail on `next` too). Installs for Claude, Codex, Kilo, Cursor, Antigravity, Windsurf, Copilot and OpenCode render the discovery steps intact. Complete per-test counts needed `RUN_TESTS_NO_FORCE_EXIT=1`: with `--test-force-exit`, run-tests truncates the TAP output of passing children, so counts vary between runs. I'll file that separately.

issue.title: enhance(#4649): scope the project-skills discovery read and report costly skills in /gsd-health

timeline.body: Correction to my status update: the `--test-force-exit` reporting loss is already tracked, as #4031 (folded into #4631) and upstream as nodejs/node#64833, whose single-file repro matches what I saw. I won't file a duplicate.

Confirming all four points from #4649 (comment 5803869317) as maintainer:

1. **Dedup via `config-get`, not `query agent-skills`** — approved. The known limitation (no project `config.json` → doesn't see `~/.gsd/defaults.json`'s `agent_skills`, skill read twice) is no worse than today's behavior, and no configured skill becomes unreachable.
2. **Generic resource-loading steps replacing the #672-pack-specific `rules/*.md` + "don't load AGENTS.md" instructions** — approved. `rules/` stays reachable through the pack's own SKILL.md references, satisfying the constraint from the original triage approval.
3. **Removing the AGENTS.md strip from both `neutralizeAgentReferences` copies** — approved. Follows directly from point 2 and fixes the empty numbered-step artifact on Codex/Copilot/Antigravity/Kimi/OpenCode/Kilo.
4. **W030 relocation to `/gsd-health` (per-skill: no description, or >500 lines) replacing the `scripts/lint-skill-deps.cjs` total-budget check** — approved. Matches the frontmatter-only read model from point 1.

Please open the PR (or proceed with review on the existing one) — this clears the scope-confirmation blocker.

issue.title: feat(#4649): scope the project-skills discovery read to task-relevant skills

timeline.body:
@trek-e Two scope questions from your review of #5079 (head `50a600d7a`), so the PR does not close this issue with part of the approved scope missing:

1. **Direction 2 (index-size budget as W030 in `/gsd-health`).** I dropped W030 from #5079. With the scoped read, an agent reads each project skill's frontmatter on every spawn and a full `SKILL.md` only when its `description` fits the task, so the per-spawn cost W030 reported is now the exception. W030 also gave `/gsd-health` a path into `buildSkillManifest`'s unbounded `SKILL.md` read (davesienkowski's `/dev/zero` repro; the pre-existing read is #5121). Proposal: move direction 2 into its own enhancement issue (a budget warning once #5121 bounds the read) and let #5079 close this one. A non-closing `Refs #4649` is not an option, because `require-issue-link` needs a closing keyword on a PR that touches source files. Alternatively I can bring W030 back into #5079. Which do you prefer?
2. **Spawn-prompt lines.** #5079 also removes the per-spawn "read every `SKILL.md`" instruction from `execute-phase.md`, `execute-phase/steps/executor-isolation-dispatch.md`, `plan-phase.md`, `quick.md` and the research capability's `plan-pre` fragment (with the regenerated `capability-registry.cjs`). Those lines told the spawned agent to read every project `SKILL.md` in full (for the executor inside `<required_reading>`), which contradicts the relevance-scoped read the agents now follow. Is that change approved within this issue, or should I split it into its own PR?

#5079 keeps `Closes #4649` until you decide; I have retitled it to drop the `/gsd-health` part.

issue.title: enhancement: execute-phase, plan-phase, quick and the research plan-pre fragment still tell agents to read every project SKILL.md
enhancement: /gsd-health warning for project skills that defeat the scoped discovery read (no description, SKILL.md over 500 lines)
